questions.question: In the study of Alkynes, what is the authoritative chemical definition of 'Alkyne'?

options.label: D
options.text: An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (-C≡C-) composed of one central σ bond and two mutually orthogonal π bonds.

questions.question: Which statement best discriminates 'Keto-Enol Tautomerism' from other related principles in Alkynes?

options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Keto-Enol Tautomerism is properly defined as: A stereoselective reduction of internal alkynes using sodium in liquid ammonia (Na/NH₃) at -78°C to yield trans-(E)-alkenes via radical anion intermediates.

options.label: B
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Keto-Enol Tautomerism specifically denotes: A chemical equilibrium between constitutional isomers that interconvert rapidly through proton migration and π-bond redistribution.

options.label: C
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Keto-Enol Tautomerism is properly defined as: A poisoned, deactivated palladium catalyst (Pd/CaCO₃/PbO) that selectively hydrogenates alkynes to cis-(Z)-alkenes via syn addition without overreduction to alkanes.

options.label: D
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Keto-Enol Tautomerism is properly defined as: An acid-catalyzed alkyne hydration using HgSO₄/H₂SO₄ that converts terminal alkynes into methyl ketones through Markovnikov addition and enol tautomerization.
